matches.rationale: Ground truth describes cherry-picked positive results and omission of failure cases in Section 4.1. Finding 2 explicitly reports exclusion of baselines, negative cases, post-hoc hyperparameter optimization, and optimistic variance, matching the same scientific issue in the same part of the paper.

Ground truth describes inconsistent specification of the projection function ψ for different meta-learners, especially ICL. No finding addresses this definitional inconsistency; Finding 1 concerns the underspecification of π_κ, which is a different technical issue.

Ground truth flags unfairness from using the same hyperparameters for all meta-learners without separate tuning, and lack of computational profiling. Finding 2 mentions post-hoc hyperparameter optimization, which is a different mechanism; no finding addresses the lack of baseline tuning or computational cost discussion.

Ground truth concerns overstated claims in the Abstract about seamless integration and significant boost given limited scope. No finding targets the Abstract or these specific rhetorical overstatements.
Ground truth notes omission of ethical considerations (environmental impact, fairness, bias) in the Discussion. None of the findings address ethical aspects or the Discussion section.

Ground truth criticizes Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 as overly strong, missing assumptions, and unproven. Finding 4 identifies exactly this exaggeration: claims of provable benefits are not rigorously supported, the proof is unrigorous, and the theoretical contribution is overstated.

Ground truth describes selective reporting of hyperparameter ablation results (K, contrastive loss variants) in Section 4.3, with negative results excluded. No finding addresses this specific ablation reporting issue.

Ground truth identifies a mismatch between the Abstract's claim of problem- and learner-agnostic generality and the method's dependence on episodic training and task identities. No finding discusses this cross-section incoherence.
Ground truth points to mischaracterization of prior works and selective citation in Related Work. None of the findings mention related work or citation practices.
Ground truth flags promotional, overstated language in the Conclusion. No finding addresses the Conclusion section or its rhetorical tone.

Ground truth highlights the ambiguous definition of the sampling strategy π_κ for inner-task distance in Section 3.1. Finding 1 directly points out that π_κ is not rigorously defined, leaving subset sizes, overlap, and sampling bias uncontrolled, matching the exact issue and location.
Ground truth notes that claims in Section 4.4 about applicability to real-world pretrained LLMs are unsupported by the synthetic experiments. No finding addresses this specific overextension to LLMs.

Ground truth warns that performance gains attributed solely to ConML are confounded by simultaneous changes in backbone architectures. No finding discusses confounded attribution from architecture changes.
Ground truth criticizes Section 4.3.2 for downplaying the sensitivity and fragility of the contrastive loss weight and distance metrics. No finding addresses this overclaim about robustness.

Ground truth reports lack of confidence intervals and statistical significance testing in experiments. Finding 3 specifically notes the absence of confidence intervals and significance tests in the reporting around Table 5, directly matching the statistical reporting deficiency.
